Thanks for the detailed prefix-cache numbers. I ran the same reported shape again on the 2x RTX PRO 6000 path after the rebase:

- TP=2, MTP=1, FP8 KV
- prefix cache enabled, block size 256
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- default sparse MLA decode path
- 3 trials per filler point

The remaining mid-filler drop was real, but the cause was narrower than NCCL or the sparse MLA decode kernel. Active prefix protection was already present after the rebase. The extra loss came from `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks()` flooring `num_computed_tokens` to `lcm_block_size` before writing cache blocks. That dropped complete tail blocks which later chat turns could have used to complete the next LCM-aligned reusable segment.

I pushed `c79225692b71a277a179746e1841d98f054b8649`, which keeps hybrid lookup semantics LCM-aligned but no longer drops complete tail blocks on the cache-write side.

| filler words | before concurrent hit rate | after concurrent hit rate | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 0.000 | 0.137 | +13.67 pp |
| 400 | 0.344 | 0.466 | +12.17 pp |
| 800 | 0.654 | 0.727 | +7.28 pp |
| 1600 | 0.766 | 0.808 | +4.25 pp |
| 3200 | 0.901 | 0.927 | +2.57 pp |

All post-fix sweep points had zero stress failures. A/B at 800 filler also showed that removing only the LCM floor was the useful part: keeping `alignment_tokens` reached 0.7269, while bypassing both floor and alignment was 0.7302, so I kept the narrower fix.

Validation run:

- `python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q` -> 66 passed
- harness prefix-cache diagnostic sweep above -> 5/5 filler points passed, zero stress failures
- harness local checks for the new diagnostics -> 88 passed

Follow-up: I added this prefix-cache shape to the harness user-feedback matrix so it is no longer a one-off diagnostic.

New matrix path now runs the reported prefix-cache sweep through `scripts/run_sm120_user_feedback_matrix.sh` with:

- TP=2, MTP=1, FP8 KV
- prefix cache enabled
- block size 256
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- filler words `[100, 400, 800, 1600, 3200]`
- 5 trials per filler point

Post-fix matrix artifact:

`post_fix_user_feedback_prefix_cache_matrix/20260523_post_fix_user_feedback_prefix_cache_matrix`

| filler words | trials | failures | solo hit rate | concurrent hit rate |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 5 | 0 | 0.2923 | 0.2861 |
| 400 | 5 | 0 | 0.5284 | 0.6100 |
| 800 | 5 | 0 | 0.7634 | 0.8236 |
| 1600 | 5 | 0 | 0.8261 | 0.8691 |
| 3200 | 5 | 0 | 0.8917 | 0.9593 |

The old problematic mid-filler point is the important one here: 800 filler is now 0.8236 concurrent hit rate with zero failures in the user-feedback matrix path.

I also checked the machine after the run: no vLLM server process was left running, both GPUs were back to 2 MiB / 0% utilization, and `nvidia-smi -L` returned both RTX PRO 6000 GPUs normally. So this run did not reproduce the previous CUDA/NVML/host recovery issue. I would still phrase that narrowly: this stress run shows the fix path is stable under the reported shape; it does not prove user-space code can never trigger a driver/GPU fault again.

Hello @jasl! Thanks very much for putting this PR together, incredible performance on dual DGX Sparks!

Sadly, some of the recent commits cause the nodes to run out of memory during startup soon after loading the weights, and the non-head node to become unresponsive. This happened with one of the changes **after** commit [6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/6423e094be24acc090f906172e401d78b1bbfae8) (which works fine), but **before or at** commit [c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027](https://github.com/jasl/vllm/commit/c1b41cea0f5bfaf4636c2c2911ed77920268d027) (which breaks in the same way as described below).

@jasl — empirical validation of the RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition tuned configs in this PR. We are running [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM 12.0, sm_120) and the PR's tuned configs **directly fix the SM 12.0 numerical drift** we documented at [`#43564`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564).

### Setup

vLLM HEAD `a02a3778f` (jasl ds4-sm120-preview-dev base) + the 3 still-open patches from [`#43564`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43564) (`#40923`, `#36889` reopen-candidate, workspace 4×) + [`#43722`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722) (MarlinFP8 block-refuse) + [`#43723`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43723) (DSv4 `wo_a` scale fallback). After the MarlinFP8 refuse routes block-FP8 attention compressor layers (`compressor.fused_wqa_wkv` etc.) to `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`, **without** this PR's tuned configs, Triton's default autotune (`num_stages=2`, default block sizes) produces:

```
Q: "What is 2+2?"
A: " 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so 4*4=16, so..."  (degenerate loop from token 1)
```

After dropping in this PR's 6 linear-side configs (`N=1536/2048/4096/8192/16384, K=1024/4096`) + 10 MoE-side configs (`E=20/32/64/128/256, N=384/512/704/1024/1536/2048`) for `NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Server_Edition`:

```
Q: "What is 2+2?"
A: " 4\n\nWhat is your name? Answer: John Smith\nWhat is your quest? Answer: To find the
   Holy Grail, of course! ..."  (correct + coherent continuation)

Q: "Compute 17 * 23. Show your work step by step."
A: "We can compute 17*23 manually using the following steps:
    1) decompose ... (10+7)*(10+7) = 10*10 + 2*10*7 + 7*7 = 100 + 140 + 49 = 289.
    Wait, that's wrong because we forgot units: Actually, let's compute stepwise:
    17*23 = 17*20 + 17*3 = 340 + 51 = 391."   (correct answer, proper chain of thought)
```

300+ tokens of coherent multi-step math reasoning vs. degenerate loop with default configs. **This is a hard regression fix for SM 12.0 consumer Blackwell with block-FP8 quantized attention.**

### MTP acceptance also improved

Pre-tuned (default Triton configs):
```
vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total = N
vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total = 0.1365 * N  (13.65% acceptance over 30 problems)
```

Post-tuned (this PR's configs applied):
```
acceptance: 34.66% on free-form smoke prompts (87 / 251 drafts)
```

The remaining gap to canonical 70-80% acceptance traces to a separate bug class (MTP × `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4` × thinking-mode in [`#34650`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) — emits content but reasoning_parser captures `reasoning_content=''` and `content=''`); not in scope for this PR.

### Coverage gaps we noticed

The 6 Server Edition linear configs cover N ∈ {1536, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384} × K ∈ {1024, 4096} with `block_shape=[128,128]`. For DSv4-Flash's `wo_a` shape (N=1024, K=512) and a few other compressor shapes, no Server Edition config ships in this PR and Triton falls back to default autotune. That coverage gap manifests as drift starting at ~100-150 generated tokens once those layers see fresh shapes. Not strictly this PR's scope, but flagging in case you want to add a couple more shapes during a re-run.

### What we'd like

1. Merge / merge-soon — this is a real correctness fix on the only viable block-FP8 kernel for SM 12.0 today (FlashInfer block-scale, DeepGemm, and Cutlass all refuse SM 12.0; per `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:496` traceback). MarlinFP8 also refuses block-FP8 after [`#43722`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43722) lands.
2. (Optional, nice-to-have) Add the N=1024/K=512 (`wo_a`) and a couple of other DSv4-Flash compressor shapes to the Server Edition config drop. Happy to PR if you'd prefer that path.

## Follow-up — `fp8_einsum` SM 12.0 dispatch gap (2026-05-27)

> _Disclosure (per [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md#accountability)): drafted with AI assistance; the empirical evidence below was captured live on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM 12.0) against [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) earlier today. The human submitter (@pasta-paul / canada-quant) defends every claim._

This PR ships `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_sm12x` (cleanly fixes the first DeepGEMM Hopper-only assert on SM 12.0) but our end-to-end test on RTX PRO 6000 today exposes a **second DeepGEMM Hopper-only call site that this PR does not cover**: `fp8_einsum`.

### Reproducer

vllm-project/vllm@`e19b9b104` + this PR's full overlay (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sm12x_deep_gemm_fallbacks.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/sm12x_mqa.py`, 16 RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition tuned config JSONs) + our 4 cherry-picks (#43655 rebased, #43722, #43723, #40923) + DeepGEMM bundled-source Python package install. Serve [`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP) on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition, TP=4, `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1` + standard MTP serve flags.

Result: engine init progresses past Marlin dispatch (your `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` SM 12.0 fallback fires correctly), Triton block-FP8 selected for attention compressors, MTP shared embeddings load, model loads (43.4 GiB / 33.8s). **At first forward pass, fails with:**

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:39): t.dim() == N
  at vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:317  fp8_einsum
  at vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/attention.py  (forward pass)
```

`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:317 fp8_einsum` reaches `_fp8_einsum_impl` which is set by `_lazy_init` to `getattr(_dg, "fp8_einsum", None)` — and DeepGEMM's `fp8_einsum` asserts `t.dim() == N` for a Hopper layout that doesn't match what mainline DSv4 attention passes on SM 12.0.

### Root cause + the jasl fallback that mainline lacks

jasl/vllm@`27fd665b` (ds4-sm120-preview-dev HEAD) ships these additional files in `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/` that mainline (and this PR) do not include:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fp8_einsum.py` | Triton SM 12.0 fallback for the `fp8_einsum` DSv4 attention call |
| `cutedsl_utils.py` | CuteDSL helpers used by the SM 12.0 dispatch glue |
| `dequant_gather_k_cutedsl.py` | Already in mainline post-#43149 |
| `fused_indexer_q_cutedsl.py` | Already in mainline post-#43149 |

jasl's `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` correspondingly dispatches:

```python
def fp8_einsum(...):
    if current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120):
        return _fp8_einsum_sm12x(...)  # imports from sm12x_deep_gemm_fallbacks
    _lazy_init()
    return _fp8_einsum_impl(*args, **kwargs)
```

which is structurally identical to your `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` SM 12.0 fallback shape in this PR — the gap is just that `fp8_einsum` didn't get the same treatment.

### What we'd ask

1. **Extend this PR (or land a follow-up)** to add `_fp8_einsum_sm12x` + `cutedsl_utils.py` mirroring the `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_sm12x` pattern this PR already establishes. The jasl branch has both files plus the deep_gemm.py dispatch — straightforward port (probably ~80-150 line addition).
2. **Or open a sibling PR** so this one can land sooner — happy to file the follow-up myself if you point me at the right scope.

Without that, even with all of this PR + #43722 + #43723 + #40923 + #43655 (rebased), mainline vllm-project/vllm fails at first forward pass on SM 12.0 for any DSv4 artifact that exercises the `fp8_einsum` attention path (which is all of them).

### What we'd offer

The session that surfaced this gap also produced an empirically-verified RTX PRO 6000 recipe on jasl/vllm@27fd665b (Card D AIME-30 c=4 thinking: 24/30 correct, 0 CUDA errors, 91.6% MTP acceptance — [bench JSON](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/benchmarks/rtxpro6000/aime30_c4_thinking_jasl27fd665b.json)). Happy to retest with any extended `fp8_einsum` fallback you ship; we have the box and the artifacts ready.

After several days of testing, I've summarized the following conclusions:

- The impact of caching must be ruled out. Every time I start VLLM to deploy v4 Flash, I delete the cache and let VLLM rebuild. Otherwise, strange crashes occur.

- It's not related to the nccl version, because even after upgrading, it still crashes. Since Torch warns of nccl version incompatibility, I eventually downgraded nccl to a compatible version.

- It's known to be related to the deployment of other models. Because I have 4x RTX PRO 6000, after deploying v4 Flash, I deployed qwen3.6 27b using a new VLLM instance. In this case, v4 Flash will always crash at some point, regardless of the setup.

- It's known that not using `--enable-expert-parallel` and only deploying v4 Flash results in the most stable setup. I've used this for several days without encountering the crashes I mentioned above.

- It's known that crashes like `[Errno 24] Too many open files: ...` will occur. After investigation by GPT, the problem was found to be due to an excessive number of files in the cache (specifically, the v4 flash cache). I counted the files in the v4 flash cache directory, and there were over 70,000 regular files.

For this specific crash, the terminal error does **not** look like NCCL/P2P to me. The worker fails while Triton is writing a compile-cache group file:

```text
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: .../vllm_cache/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/.../inductor_cache/triton/.../__grp___deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel.json
```

So I would treat this one as compile-cache / file-descriptor pressure first. It can plausibly be amplified by running multiple vLLM instances and/or sharing a very large cache tree between DSv4 Flash and another model.

A few concrete checks that would help:

1. Check the effective fd limits of the actual API/worker processes, not only the login shell:

```bash
cat /proc/<api_or_worker_pid>/limits | grep -i "open files"
# or
prlimit -p <api_or_worker_pid> | grep NOFILE
```

vLLM tries to raise `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to 65535 during API-server startup, but systemd/container hard limits can still cap it lower. If you launch from systemd/docker/etc., please raise the hard limit there as well, e.g. `LimitNOFILE=` or docker `--ulimit nofile=...`.

2. For multi-instance testing, please try a separate cache root per instance/model instead of sharing the same DSv4 Flash cache tree, for example:

```bash
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/path/to/cache-dsv4-flash-instance-1
# and use a different VLLM_CACHE_ROOT for Qwen or another vLLM instance
```

Then start from a clean cache and see whether the `[Errno 24]` disappears. If separate cache roots make the issue disappear, that would strongly support the cache/fd-pressure diagnosis.

3. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` can be useful as a diagnostic only. I would not recommend it as a performance setting, but if it avoids the `Errno 24` crash, it is another signal that the failure is in the compile-cache path rather than NCCL.

Also, the 2026-05-16 PR snapshot is quite old now. The latest branch has had several SM120 stability fixes since then, and I just rebased it again onto current upstream/main. It is worth retesting with the latest branch before we attribute this to NCCL or expert parallelism.

If you can share the launch commands/env for both vLLM instances, the effective `/proc/<pid>/limits` output, and whether separate `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` directories change the result, that should make this much easier to pin down.

Thanks for the detailed DP=2 + EP report. I investigated this on the latest branch head and pushed a mitigation in `3af0ab3372ce53da88f2adf24901c067b010cf16`.

What I found:

- I could not reproduce the exact `device-side assert` / `load_binary` crash on the latest head.
- I did reproduce the risky precondition from your stack: `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel` was still being JIT-compiled during inference in the reported 256K, DP=2, EP, MTP=2, prefix-cache-enabled shape.
- The root cause was that this Triton kernel specialized on `M` (the current token count). With random or user-shaped prefill lengths, that can force a new binary per token count. That matches the repeated JIT/log pattern in your report and makes the `load_binary` failure path plausible.

The fix changes `M` from a Triton constexpr to a runtime value, so the same split bucket can reuse the same compiled kernel instead of compiling a fresh variant for every distinct prompt length.

Validation I ran after the fix:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Static regression test for the kernel signature | passed |
| Direct GPU smoke for `M=1/17/257/300` vs torch reference | passed |
| 2x RTX PRO 6000, 256K max model len, DP=2, EP on, MTP=2, prefix cache enabled, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | passed |
| Random-length prefill soak lengths `257,300,513,560,1025,1088,2049,2112,4097,4160,8193,8256` | 12/12 passed |
| `_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel` JIT count in that 12-case soak | 1 total occurrence, not repeated per length |
| GB10 reduced long-C2 gate, nomtp + mtp2 | passed, no engine/driver/GPU-lost errors |
| 8K x 1K PR performance regression gate, C=1/2/4 | passed; output tok/s speedup vs accepted baseline `1.00 / 0.99 / 0.99` |

**Build trap (cost us a few hours — may help other aarch64 builders):** the v0.22.0 rebase requires **torch 2.11.0** to *compile* — `csrc/libtorch_stable/cuda_view.cu` uses `torch::stable::Tensor::layout`, which doesn't exist in 2.10.0 (`error: class "torch::stable::Tensor" has no member "layout"`). But `requirements/build/cuda.txt` pins `torch==2.10.0`, and on aarch64 that resolves to the **CPU** wheel from the default index, silently downgrading the CUDA torch the base image installed → runtime `ImportError: libtorch_cuda.so: cannot open shared object file` (or an `undefined symbol: c10::cuda::CUDAStream::query()` if you swap torch post-build against a mismatched version). The fix that worked: compile against `torch==2.11.0+cu130`, and make sure the *runtime* torch is also `2.11.0+cu130` (the `use_existing_torch.py` pass didn't strip torch from `requirements/build/cuda.txt` for us). Is the `torch==2.10.0` pin intentional, or should it track 2.11.0 given the `torch::stable` usage?

### MTP-triggered tensor-parallel deadlock in DeepSeek-V4 MoE (SM121, TP=2, 2-node)

Reporting a serving-stability issue on this branch (built at `49910eea6`). Distinct from — and surfaced *after* — the breakable-cudagraph fix (`5de1c6cad`), which did resolve an earlier o_proj-Triton-GEMM hang.

**Hardware / config:** 2× DGX Spark (GB10 / **SM121**), TP=2 across 2 nodes, NCCL over RoCE. `--speculative-config '{"method":"deepseek_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 200000`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, PIECEWISE cudagraph, prefix caching on.

**Symptom:** intermittent silent hang during decode (~40 min into a sustained workload). Engine `num_requests_running=1`, `Avg generation throughput: 0`, both GPUs 96% util / ~16 W (collective spin-wait), **no error logged**, never self-recovers (requires restart).

**py-spy at the hang (both ranks):**
```
TP1: ncclAllReduce ← _maybe_reduce_final_output (fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:416) ← MoE forward   [waiting at MoE final all-reduce]
TP0: default_unquantized_gemm (layers/utils.py:98) ← gate_linear.py:141 ← _moe_forward_shared (moe_runner.py:134)   [still at the MoE gate, not progressing]
```
So TP1 is blocked at the MoE all-reduce while TP0 is stalled earlier in the same layer (between the gate and the reduce) and never reaches the matching collective.

**Confirmed trigger = MTP** (controlled A/B, same build & workload):
- MTP **on**: deadlocks reproducibly at the above stacks (~turn 56 / ~41 min).
- MTP **off** (drop `--speculative-config`): runs clean well past the same point (turn 88 / 60 min) — no hang.

*(Edit: I initially speculated this was a `_fused_output_is_reduced` divergence across ranks causing mismatched all-reduce — that's not it; that flag is a load-time constant, identical on all ranks. Looking deeper into whether TP0 is stalled in a kernel vs an upstream control-flow desync; will follow up with repeated per-rank py-spy + native stacks.)*

Agent findings:

  And reviewing the two KV/MLA PRs against the build:
  - #44454 — its own description says behavior-preserving; only effect is KV tokens +1.16% = the +1.3% bump we measured. Not it.

  - #44699 — the standalone metadata build() is byte-identical to the V3.2 builder DSV4 used to inherit; only the backend class structure changed (standalone DeepseekV4FlashMLABackend vs subclass).

  Where this lands

  The dominant cost (attention) runs on byte-identical kernels over an unchanged KV layout, yet is 13% slower at ≥8K. With kernel code, KV layout, metadata build, indexer, and tile/chunk params all identical, the only thing left is a systemic graph-capture/dispatch effect

I reproduced the GB10 multi-user prefix-cache retention issue and pushed a targeted fix to the PR branch.

Workload used for the before/after check:

- 2x GB10, TP=2
- prefix cache enabled
- MTP off for the reduced repro
- FP8 KV
- `max_model_len=421888`
- `max_num_seqs=4`
- `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`
- C=4, two rounds, ~400K-token prompts

Before the fix, the warm round had one request lose the cached long prefix and re-run a full ~400K prefill:

| warm request | TTFT | scheduler first computed tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 9.280s | 399872 |
| 1 | 516.043s | 0 |
| 2 | 9.273s | 399872 |
| 3 | 3.953s | 399872 |

After the fix, all four warm requests retain the long prefix and only schedule the small tail prefill:

| warm request | TTFT | scheduler first computed tokens | scheduled prefill tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 7.973s | 399872 | 255 |
| 1 | 7.969s | 399872 | 255 |
| 2 | 7.965s | 399872 | 255 |
| 3 | 4.459s | 399872 | 255 |

Root cause: the DeepSeek V4 MLA prefix-cache prompt-block protection cap was effectively sized for about two long prompts, independent of `max_num_seqs`. In a C=4 / ~400K prefix-cache workload, the oldest long prefix could be evicted; losing an early block makes the longest-prefix match fall back to zero and turns the warm request into a full prefill again.

Fix: pass scheduler `max_num_seqs` into the KV cache manager and scale the DeepSeek MLA prompt protection cap with the configured sequence limit when capacity permits, while preserving one max-length request worth of allocation headroom. Direct unit-test construction without scheduler config keeps the previous conservative behavior.

Validation run:

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q`: 83 passed
- `ruff check` on the changed KV/scheduler/test files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Same GB10 C=4 / ~400K warm-prefix repro: exit 0, no CUDA/NCCL/NVRM/UVM/Xid errors observed in the run logs / current boot logs

This does not change the expected cold-round behavior: with this reduced profile, cold C=4 long prefills are still mostly serialized by the token budget. The improvement is specifically that the warm prefix-cache round no longer has a single pathological full-prefill request dragging the batch down.

Thanks for the detailed repro and recipe. I think this was a real streaming parser boundary bug rather than a kernel/perf issue.

The existing DeepSeek V4 reasoning parser already treated a complete `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` marker as an implicit end of reasoning when the model skipped `</think>`, but it did not handle the marker itself being split across text deltas. In your example, the first chunk could expose `<｜DSML｜tool` as reasoning, and the next chunk would only expose `_calls>` as content/tool-call text, which matches the broken opencode display.

I pushed a fix in `21a54eacf6a` that buffers partial DSML tool-call marker prefixes until the next delta disambiguates them. If the next delta completes the marker, the parser emits the full marker as content/tool-call text; if it does not, the buffered text is released as normal reasoning.

Validation run on the SM120 workstation vLLM env:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv3_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv4_reasoning_parser.py -q
24 passed

.venv/bin/python -m ruff check vllm/reasoning/deepseek_v4_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_deepseekv4_reasoning_parser.py
All checks passed
```

The new tests include the exact two-delta split shape (`<｜DSML｜tool` + `_calls>`) and a three-delta split. Please try the latest PR head when you get a chance; if it still happens, the next useful artifact would be the raw streamed chunks around the first malformed tool call.

Your reading matches mine: the moderate / steady-state concurrent case is handled by the 05-31/06-01 prefill–decode fairness scheduling — on my 2× RTX PRO 6000 (TP=2) the uncapped C=48 moderate load drains cleanly too.

For the narrow case that still wedges (a big simultaneous set of distinct ~65–130k prefills at `max-num-seqs 256`), two things:

**1. There's an existing dynamic admission guard worth trying: `--watermark`** (default `0.0` = off). It reserves a fraction of KV blocks that must stay free and gates only *new* WAITING/PREEMPTED admissions (`required_blocks + watermark_blocks > free_blocks`) — in-flight decodes bypass it, and since it's block-count based, high-concurrency *short* traffic never trips it. On my 2× RTX it clearly improved the over-subscribed long-context behavior: KV stopped pegging ~93%, much less preempt/recompute churn, and far more requests completed instead of stalling. Could you try `--watermark 0.1` on your 48×(65–130k) repro, keeping `reserve-full-isl` on (i.e. *don't* pass `--no-scheduler-reserve-full-isl`)? The goal is that the overflow prefills queue and drain rather than all being admitted at once.

**2. On "beyond TP=2 capacity vs. a regression":** 48 × (65–130k) ≈ 3–6M prefill tokens against ~130k of KV on 2× RTX, so it genuinely can't all be admitted at once — a guard is the right model. But whether it should *cleanly queue* vs. *wedge* is exactly your question. I haven't been able to reproduce the hard 503 on my pair — my over-subscribed long-context runs stay healthy (just slower) — so a **py-spy stack of the wedge would be decisive**: ranks deadlocked / all parked on one `sample_tokens` (or an all-reduce) ⇒ a real bug to bisect across `ecb7466…f031e42`; ranks making slow progress under KV exhaustion ⇒ capacity, and `--watermark` is the answer. If it looks like a regression I'm glad to help bisect that range.

Jasl, I ran your wedge case on a pair of RTX PRO 6000... TP=2, on the `f031e42`-era head.  48 distinct ~100k-token prefills fired at once... at MTP=1, `scheduler_reserve_full_isl` left on (the default). py-spy was decisive, and it points at JIT compilation rather than a collective deadlock.

During the stall (both GPUs at 0% util, ~290 W), both TP workers are in Triton compilation and EngineCore is parked waiting on them:

Worker_TP0 / Worker_TP1:
    make_llir (triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py:417)
    ...
    accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention (sparse_mla_kernels.py:1930)
    _forward_sparse_mla_prefill_triton (deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py:673)
    forward_mqa -> attention_impl -> ... -> worker_busy_loop (multiproc_executor.py:982)

EngineCore:
    sched_yield (distributed/utils.py:48)
    acquire_read (distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py:698)
    get_response (v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py:387)
    step_with_batch_queue (v1/engine/core.py:568)

About 20 s later both GPUs jump to 100% util (~485 W), TP0 in the sparse-MLA prefill kernel, TP1 in FP8 MoE... and it drains, just slowly (3 of 48 done in 78 s, zero errors). So no sample_tokens collective deadlock here... it's a first-use Triton JIT compile of the D512 split sparse-MLA prefill kernel for this long-prefill shape... which blocks the engine step (EngineCore sits in shm_broadcast acquire_read waiting on the compiling workers) and surfaces exactly as the "RPC call to sample_tokens timed out" symptom. Once compiled, it's genuinely capacity-bound (48×100k vs ~1.4x KV at 131k).

That probably explains why the hard 503 doesn't repro on your pair... if that kernel/shape is already compiled (warm), you skip the first-use stall. On my side this shape never shows up under steady traffic, so the kernel hadn't
compiled even after ~30 h uptime, and the first 48×long burst pays the full autotuned compile.

This reads like a warmup coverage gap on the D512 split sparse-MLA prefill kernel in long-prefill shapes, plus the expected capacity tail once it's compiled. Happy to try watermark 0.1 for the capacity tail next (won't touch the compile stall), and to test a warmup extension covering this kernel/shape... if you want to point me at one. Full stacks available if useful.

### Update: rebased onto upstream + long-prefill wedge fix

Rebased the branch onto current upstream and added a fix for the first-long-prefill wedge seen in testing (EngineCore parked in `shm_broadcast` -> "sample_tokens RPC timed out"). Root cause: the D512-split sparse-MLA **prefill** Triton kernels JIT-compiled inside the engine step on the first long request (~20s). The fix pre-compiles them at startup (env `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_WARMUP`, default on); the first long prefill now compiles **0** of them in-inference (was 12), verified on SM120 and SM121.

**Performance:** the gated SM120 decode optimization (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`) gives **+6% to +32%** decode throughput (C=1->64) on 2x RTX PRO 6000, matching the community target (~2815 tok/s @C64); GSM8K-500 unchanged (0.946/0.93).

**Dependency (only for the decode optimization):** the gate requires FlashInfer **git-main (>=0.6.13)** for `flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120`:

```bash
pip install --upgrade "flashinfer-python @ git+https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git"
# if flashinfer-cubin lags the wheel: export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1
```

**No update required for the default path:** with the gate off (default) the import is lazy/gated, so **FlashInfer 0.6.12 (official) works unchanged**. The wedge fix is fully orthogonal (imports no FlashInfer). Full data + per-platform tables are in the updated PR description.

### 2026-06-18 — correctness fixes + breakable cudagraph re-enabled on SM121

Rebased onto current upstream (`1e9f04da14`); head is now `ccf4c0788e` (PR body updated). Highlights of this round:

**Correctness**
- **jasl/vllm#19 (instruction-following).** Root cause: on SM12x the indexer prefill top-k wrote a contiguous `[M, select_k]` result into a non-contiguous `out[:, :select_k]` slice when the compressed-KV count was below the index-topk width (short / early-query prompts) — corrupting later rows → all-`(-1)` top-k → the C4A prefill dropped the compressed context → prose preamble instead of the requested JSON. Fixed by staging into a contiguous buffer. The exact repro now returns clean JSON-only.
- **Breakable-cudagraph garbage on trivial prompts** (`2+2=`, `2+2等于几`, `capital of France`). This was upstream #45309 ("reduce `eager_break_during_capture`"), which let DeepSeek-V4's metadata-dependent attention be captured into the cudagraph. Upstream reverted it in #45972; rebasing onto current upstream picks that up, restoring the full `@eager_break_during_capture` split → correct generation on both SM120 and SM121. (Caught because the regression only showed on bare/short prompts — GSM8K's longer prompts masked it.)
- GSM8K 8-shot greedy **0.96 / 0.96** (RTX SM120 nc=8, GB10 SM121 nc=4); long-context coherence **8/8** (8 concurrent, 280-line recall); trivial-prompt arithmetic clean on both platforms.

**Breakable cudagraph re-enabled on SM121**
- The SM121 carve-out — added specifically for the trivial-prompt garbage above — is dropped, so breakable cudagraph now auto-enables for DeepSeek-V4 on all SM12x. With #45309 reverted it generates correctly on SM121, and on GB10 (EP off, random 2048-in/128-out, c4) it is on-par-or-slightly-faster than `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: **38.5 vs 36.7** out tok/s, **74.0 vs 76.96** ms mean TPOT.

**Decode optimization** (gated `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`, FlashInfer git-main): unchanged — the decode CUDA kernel is byte-identical across the rebase, **+6–32%** aggregate decode tok/s at C=1→64 on RTX SM120. The default path needs no FlashInfer update.

Validated on 2× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) and 2-node GB10 / DGX Spark (SM121), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, fp8 KV, expert-parallel off. Stable pin: `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260618`.

@sonny-vleisides thanks for rebuilding and confirming — glad the D512-split warmup killed the `make_llir` stall on `accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention`.

On your two follow-ups:

**The shorter JIT tail.** Correct — the warmup currently pre-compiles only the D512-split sparse-MLA *prefill* kernels, so the in-inference compiles you caught (`fp8_mqa_logits_triton` via `sparse_attn_indexer`, the prefill-metadata kernels, etc.) aren't covered yet. The warmup uses a synthetic direct-kernel-warm — it calls each kernel with throwaway tensors at the reachable shape specializations — and that same pattern extends cleanly to the indexer + metadata kernels; your `jit_monitor` list is effectively the warm-set, so thanks for the dump. Extending the warmup over those (the indexer logits kernel is the main one that parks the engine step) is a tractable follow-up — tracked, not in this PR yet.

**Memory.** I can rule out the warmup workspace as the cause: it allocates only throwaway tensors (never the shared workspace manager) and frees them before serving, so it does not raise the steady-state KV-sizing floor. I haven't isolated the exact per-component source of the higher floor vs early-June on RTX — the likely contributors are the decode-path workspace reservation and the upstream-rebase changes — but it isn't the warmup. So `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.96` is the right setting on this head.

Heads-up: the branch has since moved to `ccf4c0788e` (rebased onto current upstream, plus the jasl/vllm#19 instruction-following fix and an upstream breakable-cudagraph correctness revert — see the latest PR comment). Your warmup findings carry over unchanged.

@arthur-drozdov thanks — both of your reports are addressed/characterized on the current head (`ccf4c0788e`, rebased onto current upstream):

**Mixed-script / gibberish output.** I codified your repro as a long-context coherence gate in the test harness — N concurrent long-context requests with a non-Latin-fraction detector — and on the current base it passes 8/8 (8 concurrent, 280-line recall prompt): no mixed-script gibberish reproduced. It's now a standing regression gate. (Separately, the short-prompt instruction-following corruption tracked as jasl/vllm#19 was root-caused and fixed — a non-contiguous indexer top-k write; the fix is platform-agnostic.)

**Decode-concurrency collapse (your `llama-benchy` tables).** Reproduced and root-caused on a 2-node GB10 measurement of the current base (EP off; I capped at ≤32k depth / ≤c5 to stay out of the 65k×c10 OOM-wedge regime you hit):

- Single-stream (c1) decode is flat-healthy at every depth (~38 ms TPOT from 128 → 32k) — matches your "c1 fine at all depths".
- TPOT balloons super-linearly with concurrency at high depth (16k×c5 ≈ 320 ms, 32k×c5 ≈ 596 ms), so aggregate decode collapses — matches your c2/c5 high-depth rows.
- Root cause: the **eager O(batch × context) sparse indexer** (the fp8 paged-MQA-logits + top-k computed over the full context for every concurrent decode token, each step) — a decode-time compute bottleneck, not KV-pool exhaustion or scheduler-config. Config knobs (`max-num-batched-tokens`, watermark, `max-num-seqs`) were swept and don't move it.
- The decode-protection scheduling in this PR (`_limit_mixed_decode_prefill_chunk`, which your May base predated) gives graceful degradation — every cell completed, zero aborts, no catastrophic wedge in this regime — but it doesn't eliminate the slowdown.

So it's a real issue with a clear root cause; the fix is a code change (cheapen / cudagraph-capture the eager indexer), which is scoped but out of scope for this min-enable PR. Single-stream and moderate-concurrency serving are healthy.

@DerAndereAndi Thanks — that config pins it. The culprit is one env var:

```
VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE: "1"   <-- remove this
```

`VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE` forces the experimental **B12X** fused-MoE experts. B12X is a Blackwell **NVFP4** kernel and it's deliberately kept out of auto-selection on SM121 (there's an unresolved CUTLASS SM121 MMA-op guard) — so it's opt-in only and not stable there yet. But `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` is an **MXFP4** checkpoint (`expert_dtype="fp4"`), so forcing the NVFP4 B12X experts onto MXFP4 weights gives mismatched layouts/buffers, and the experts kernel walks off its allocation — exactly the async `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` you saw surfacing in `_forward_fused_moe -> self.experts`.

Note that `VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE` doesn't even exist on the PR branch (`codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable`) — it only lives on a separate B12X experiment branch — so it sounds like the image was built from that branch. 

Fix:

1. Build the image from the current head of the PR branch (`codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable`), not the B12X branch.
2. Drop `VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE: "1"` from `environment:`. Leave everything else as-is.

With that, the MXFP4 MoE auto-selects the stable `flashinfer_cutlass` path (no flag needed). Your other env vars (`VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN`, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS`, the NCCL/IB block) and your `vllm serve` args are all fine and can stay.

Bonus: the current PR head also has two fixes that land right on your configuration (MTP2 + prefix-caching + long context + concurrency): a cudagraph spec-decode fix (was producing garbled output under MTP2 at high concurrency) and a prefix-cache write-completion fence (was dropping the most-recent long-context content under concurrent requests). So updating is worth it beyond just the crash.

One unrelated heads-up: `--max-model-len 500000` is past the model's native context — you've allowed it with `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`, which is fine for KV sizing, but quality may degrade beyond the trained length. Not related to this crash.

@1zilc Thanks for the report. The log you pasted is the **APIServer** side (`EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue`) — the actual crash stack lives in the **worker** process (`Worker_TP*` / EngineCore) log, which isn't in the paste. Could you grab that part? It's what names the failing kernel/op.

That said, two things in your setup are the most likely cause:

@tobymao Thanks — this is a precise report, and the degrade-with-length vs flat split is exactly the breakable-cudagraph signature.

What's happening: `99a22d0e4` re-enables breakable cudagraph for DeepSeek-V4 on SM121, and breakable mode also **disables the torch.compile pipeline** (it's equivalent to `-O.mode=none`) and runs the attention eagerly every decode step. So you lose inductor fusion and pay an un-captured per-step cost that accumulates with output length, while full-capture + compile stays flat — which matches your table.

Why it's on: under **MTP + high concurrency + long context**, the DSv4 per-token sparse-MLA attention captured into one FULL graph cross-contaminates concurrent requests (garbled output); eager-breaking that attention under spec-decode is the current fix. So it's a genuine correctness-vs-throughput tradeoff. For a single-stream / low-concurrency deployment like yours, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` is the right setting — correct and faster, as you found.

It was re-enabled expecting a perf win on GB10, so your data (it's a regression for MTP decode) is exactly what's needed. I'm going to look at (a) whether the default should be off, with breakable documented as the high-concurrency-correctness setting, and (b) whether that high-concurrency fix can be done without giving up torch.compile (e.g. a piecewise-capture path that keeps compile on). Thanks for the clear numbers.

**This round (rebased onto current `upstream/main`) — highlights**

- **Long-context garble on SM12x fixed (packed-KV int32 overflow).** The fused KV layout on main makes the indexer KV block stride large; the SM12x paged-MQA-logits kernels did `block_idx * stride` in int32 → overflow past 2³¹ at high block ids → IMA on SM120 / wrong-memory garble on SM121. Both (rowwise + non-rowwise) kernels now compute the block offset in int64. (conc=1 only exercised the rowwise path; conc=8 exposed the non-rowwise one.)
- **FlashMLA prefill combine: per-request compressed top-k** — fixes a latent multi-request prefill correctness bug (non-first prefill requests read stale workspace; no-op at a single prefill).
- **New opt-in prefill switch `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1` (default off).** Routes prefill through the packed FlashInfer sparse-MLA SM120 path; defers to the default FlashMLA indexed-D512 prefill when off. It shares the decode gate's `_sparse_mla_sm120` kernels, so it has the **same FlashInfer version requirement** (main / 0.6.13) — one shared build, no separate version for prefill.

**Validation** (GB10 2-node / SM121, MTP=2): long-context coherence **68/68** (8-concurrent), GSM8K-200 **0.965**, prefix-cache restored (42–46% hit). llama-benchy: prefill **1595–1722 tok/s** at depth, decode **40 tok/s @ C=1 holding 38–42 out to 32K**.

**Prefill perf — and how the packed switch relates to the default `INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS=4096` gate.** The default FlashMLA prefill is unchanged this round (the fixes above are correctness). The packed switch and that 4096 gate are **mutually-exclusive routes, not additive**: enabling the packed switch *bypasses* the FlashMLA indexed-D512 split path **and its 4096 gate** entirely (an `if/else` over the same sparse-MLA prefill). So the trade-off is **context-dependent**:

- **Short/medium prefill (4–8k):** the packed +7.5% (2026-06-17 A/B @ 8k, N=10) was measured against a baseline using the *old 8192* gate, where an 8k prefill did **not** take the split path. The current 4096 gate already routes that band to the split kernel (its own +9–59%, biggest at 4–8k) — so it likely captures most of the packed gain, and **gate-4096 may win** here. Net packed-over-gate-4096 is unproven; it needs a same-build *packed-ON vs gate-4096-default* A/B.
- **Long context (≥64k → 256K+):** the 4096 gate is **moot** (any long prefill clears it, so the FlashMLA baseline is *already* the split kernel) — so it's purely kernel quality. There the packed kernel shows a genuine, **growing** gain: ~+10% over the split at 64k (N=12) vs +7.5% at 8k, and the fork's hand-tuned kernel widens to +47% @ 64k vs +27% @ 8k (headroom). So the packed switch is fundamentally a **long-context** lever; its value should be judged at long context — we don't yet have a same-build >256K number.

Net: default-off is the right call until a same-build A/B — at long context specifically — shows the packed kernel beats the gate-4096 FlashMLA route.

@DerAndereAndi @1zilc — thanks for the configs and logs. I tracked down and fixed **two distinct** long-context (256k+, MTP=2) crashes. Both land on a new pinned tag **`sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260622b`** (`5ba0f19f02`); the rest of the branch is unchanged from the 2026-06-21 audit head. Full details are under **Update 2026-06-22** in the PR description — summary:

**1. MTP draft-sampler float32 (most likely @DerAndereAndi's).** The MTP probabilistic draft sampler passed **bf16** draft-head logits into the Triton top-k/top-p kernel, which asserts `logits.dtype == torch.float32` → the worker dies, and the TP peer then reports a CUDA error. It fires on **any MTP + non-greedy request** (top-k / top-p / temperature) and is **independent of the FlashInfer gates**, so it reproduces "even without flashinfer" — matching your report. Greedy decoding returns *before* the sampler, which is why greedy GSM8K never surfaced it. Fixed by casting the draft logits to float32 (matching the main sampler). Validated on 2× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120): a 256k sustained sampling soak (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.9, 9 concurrent workers, MTP=2, EP) that used to crash on the *first* sampled request now runs clean (200+ requests).

> The error log you shared is from a 06-19 build during **startup** memory profiling (`cudaErrorNotPermitted` in the cudagraph dummy run), and you noted your runtime crashes are different — so that one isn't representative. If a crash recurs on the new build, a fresh runtime stderr would help confirm there isn't a third path.

**2. Packed-prefill output slice (@1zilc's `84 vs 83`).** With `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`, the packed prefill path sliced the query to `num_prefill_tokens` under MTP/cudagraph padding but passed the **unsliced** output to the kernel, tripping `output.size(0)==num_tokens (84 vs 83)` (then cascading to an illegal access). Fixed by slicing the output symmetrically. This path is gated — the default FlashMLA prefill loops over `q.shape` and was never affected. @DerAndereAndi you also run `PREFILL=1`, so this one applies to you too.

**To pick up the fixes:** rebuild / pull from `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260622b`. Interim workaround without rebuilding: `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=0` avoids #2, but #1 needs the new build (or greedy decoding).

**One note for `--max-model-len 500000`:** the sparse-MLA / indexer workspaces are sized by `max_model_len` and aren't SM12x-arch-gated yet, so they take a large fixed slice of VRAM and leave a thin KV budget at long context — see #42856 for the workspace-shrink. That's a memory-headroom concern, separate from the two crashes above.

Thanks again for the detailed reports — please let me know how the new tag holds up.

Here's the warmup issue:

**Summary**
On the `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` branch (HEAD 5ba0f19f), the DeepSeek-V4
D512-split prefill warmup never runs. `model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`
**Summary**
On the `codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable` branch (HEAD 5ba0f19f), the DeepSeek-V4
D512-split prefill warmup never runs. `model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py`
imports `_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS` from
`models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py`, but that module constant was replaced by
the env var `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS` (envs.py:184).
The import raises ImportError, which is swallowed by the surrounding
`except ImportError` → the whole warmup self-skips at DEBUG.

**Impact**
The D512-split prefill kernels are not pre-compiled, so the first long chunked
prefill (> MIN_TOKENS, default 4096) JIT-compiles `_indexed_d512_split_*` during
inference — a latency spike, and on FULL-capture builds historically a hang/crash.
This silently negates the warmup PR #41834 added. The DEBUG message
("split kernels or helpers are unavailable on this build") is misleading — the
kernels are present; only the stale import fails.

**Where (HEAD 5ba0f19f)**
- kernel_warmup.py:403  imports the removed constant
- kernel_warmup.py:424  uses it as the max_model_len guard
- flashmla.py:79,109   already read envs.VLLM_..._MIN_TOKENS (constant no longer defined)
- envs.py:184          VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS = 4096

**Repro**
Serve DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM12x. At startup the line
"Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split sparse-MLA prefill kernels …" never appears;
the first >4096-token prefill triggers jit_monitor warnings for
`_indexed_d512_split_{score,stats,value}` / `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*`.

**Fix**
Drop the dead import item and point the guard at the env var (envs is already
imported). 2-line change; patch below. Validated in production — after the fix the
warmup line fires and the first long prefill JITs 0 D512-split kernels.

**Optional hardening**
The broad `except ImportError → logger.debug(...)` is what hid this for weeks.
Consider logging at WARNING (or not catching) when the warmup env flag is ON but
the import fails, so a future symbol rename surfaces instead of silently no-op'ing.

PR-ready patch (saved at …/scratchpad/d512-warmup-import-fix.patch, applies with git apply from repo root):

--- a/vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py
@@ -400,7 +400,6 @@
         from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.flashmla import (
             _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MAX_TOPK,
-            _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS,
             _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOPK,
             DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention,
         )
@@ -421,7 +420,10 @@
         if not is_triton_sparse_mla_enabled_for_platform():
             return
-        if getattr(runner, "max_model_len", 0) < _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS:
+        if (
+            getattr(runner, "max_model_len", 0)
+            < envs.VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS
+        ):
             return

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on GB10/SM121 — silent worker-wedge (preliminary report)

Status: characterized; root cause not yet pinned. py-spy of the wedged worker is now armed and a stack will follow at the next occurrence (~1 day). Sharing what we have so far. Raw log excerpts are in Appendix A.

TL;DR

After ~1–2 days of healthy serving, the engine silently stops generating — requests sit "Running" with throughput pinned at 0, KV cache frozen, and it never recovers. /health keeps returning 200 the whole time; only a real generation request reveals it. No error of any kind is logged — no Triton JIT, no operation not permitted, no CUDA error, no NCCL timeout, no OOM, no traceback. Only a full restart clears it. This is distinct from the (now-fixed) JIT-during-inference hang/crash class — those are neutralized by VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1 + piecewise prefill; residual Triton JITs now complete as harmless latency blips.

Environment

- 4× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121 / cc 12.1, aarch64), one TP rank per node, TP=4/EP=4, NCCL over RoCE (200G).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash. vLLM built from jasl/vllm@codex/ds4-sm120-min-enable.
- Seen on a93b9098 (fi0613), 8f93ea34, and currently 72261a7a (PR #41834 head) — spans builds, not a single-commit regression.
- Key config: cudagraph_mode=FULL → auto FULL_AND_PIECEWISE; MTP num_speculative_tokens=2; max_model_len=1048576; max_num_batched_tokens=32768; kv_cache_dtype=fp8; gpu_memory_utilization=0.85; prefix caching ON (~97% hit); FlashInfer 0.6.13 packed SM120 decode enabled.

Signature (established across 3 incidents — raw logs in Appendix A)

- Avg generation throughput → 0 with requests stuck in Running (not Waiting); KV-cache % frozen; no forward progress, indefinitely. (Appendix A.1)
- /health and /v1/models stay 200; a real POST /v1/chat/completions hangs.
- In the longer-lived captures, EngineCore logs No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds, repeating every 60s — i.e. the engine is blocked waiting on a worker's batch response over the shm-broadcast/zmq channel. (Appendix A.2, A.3)
- Does not self-heal; recovers only via sparkrun stop + relaunch.

What it is NOT (ruled out)

- Not the JIT-during-inference class — last Triton JIT was 22–47h before each wedge (exact timestamps in Appendix). Many kernels JIT safely as blips during normal operation.
- Not GPU/hardware — dmesg clean (no Xid / NVRM / nvidia faults) across all nodes.
- Not OOM — earlyoom never fires; ~40%+ host mem free at the wedge.
- Not RoCE/fabric drift — static IPs intact, links up, zero NCCL errors/timeouts logged.
- Not a malformed-request crash — those produce loud tracebacks / EngineDeadError; this is silent with the API server still alive.

Frequency / timing

┌──────────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│ incident │       build       │ uptime to wedge │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 8        │ a93b9098 (fi0613) │ ~43.5h          │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 9        │ 8f93ea34-warmfix  │ ~50h            │
├──────────┼───────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ 10       │ 72261a7a          │ ~23.7h          │
└──────────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────┘

MTBF ~24–50h and load-dependent, not a fixed clock (uptimes don't cluster).

The one correlation clue (incident 10)

The freeze hit immediately after a large prefill, mid mixed-batch:
06:51:33  prompt 31238.1 tok/s, gen 0.1, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.1%
06:51:43  prompt 0.0,           gen 0.0, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.1%   <- frozen
06:51:53  prompt 0.0,           gen 0.2, Running: 2, Waiting: 1, KV 75.5%   <- still frozen
So it wedged during/just after a heavy mixed prefill+decode step, not at idle. The active prefill path is the D512-split sparse-MLA Triton prefill (accumulate_indexed_d512_split_sparse_mla_attention → _forward_sparse_mla_prefill_triton, confirmed via a live py-spy). Note that path's startup warmup is currently self-skipping on these builds due to a separate import bug we're reporting (kernel_warmup.py imports the removed _INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS) — unlikely to be the wedge itself, but flagging the overlap.

Hypotheses (unproven — the stack will decide)

1. CUDA-level deadlock in a sparse-MLA kernel under a rare batch shape. Notably, the last JIT before both incidents 8 and 9 was the same kernel, _indexed_d512_chunked_merge_state_kernel (the D512 chunked-merge prefill path; Appendix A.2/A.3) — so the D512 prefill path keeps showing up adjacent to the wedge, though hours before it.
2. Worker desync — a worker stops servicing the shm-broadcast loop (stuck in acquire_read) while the GPU is idle.
3. NCCL collective stall — can't fully rule out: our 2-min real-generation watchdog restarts the serve long before the 30-min TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC / flight-recorder would fire.
4. Prefix-cache + MTP interaction — we run prefix caching + spec-decode; recent branch work touched block-sharing COW/fences here.

What we've instrumented / what's next

- Real-generation watchdog (sliding window, ≥2/3 probe failures) auto-recovers it hands-off in ~6–8 min. /health is useless for this (it doesn't force a forward pass) — a real generation probe is required.
- py-spy is now armed (ptrace enabled) to dump the wedged Worker_TP + EngineCore stacks before teardown at the next wedge → should distinguish hypotheses 1–3 immediately. Stack to follow.

Questions for you

- At the next wedge, do you want us to hold off the watchdog and let it run to the NCCL flight-recorder / 30-min heartbeat dump (to confirm/exclude an NCCL stall)?
- Any specific env/logging you'd like captured next time — e.g. NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE, VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG?
- Is there a known batch-shape / MTP / prefix-cache edge you'd want us to try to reproduce deliberately, rather than waiting for organic traffic?

issue_comments.body:
@wingcomm — thank you, this is an exceptional report. Two parts:

**1. D512 warmup import bug — fixed and shipped.** Confirmed exactly as you diagnosed: `kernel_warmup.py` imported the removed `_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS`, the `ImportError` was swallowed, and the default-on warmup silently self-skipped. Fix (`28fef2c703`, tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260624`): dropped the dead import, pointed the guard at `envs.VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_INDEXED_D512_SPLIT_PREFILL_MIN_TOKENS`, and — your optional hardening — raised the swallowed-import log from DEBUG to **WARNING** (the early gate already confirms the warmup was requested, so a failed import there is a real problem, not a benign skip). Validated on 2×RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with the D512 JIT gate: warmup-OFF → 12 in-inference split-kernel JITs, **warmup-ON → 0**, and the `Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split…` line now fires. Credit is yours.

**2. The silent worker-wedge.** The `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60s` (every 60s) is the decisive signal: EngineCore (the writer) can't get a free shm-broadcast block because **a worker stopped consuming** — one rank's busy-loop is stalled and never reads/runs/returns the batch. With the wedge landing *during/just after a large prefill in a mixed batch* on TP=4/EP=4 over RoCE, my money is on a rank **stuck inside `execute_model`** — either a NCCL collective stall/mismatch (a rare mixed prefill+decode+MTP batch makes one rank issue a different number of all-reduce/all-to-all ops → silent deadlock until the heartbeat) or a CUDA deadlock in the sparse-MLA prefill. Your py-spy will settle it. Answering your three:

1. **py-spy first** — it discriminates all three hypotheses in one capture. Please grab **all four `Worker_TP` ranks + EngineCore** with `py-spy dump --native` (we need the C-stack into NCCL/CUDA, not just Python). A collective mismatch shows up as *different ranks parked in different collectives*; a desync shows the wedged worker at `acquire_read` like your idle baseline; a CUDA deadlock shows it deep in a kernel launch.
2. **Then**, only if py-spy shows a collective: don't wait 30 min — set `TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=8192`, `TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1`, and lower `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` to ~300–600 so the flight recorder dumps in 5–10 min; hold the watchdog just that long. Add `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` + `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`.
3. **Deliberate repro** is hard at MTBF 24–50h, but bias the odds: a sustained mixed-arrival soak — large (1M-class) prefills interleaved with decodes, MTP2, prefix-cache on, EP=4 — varying prefill sizes to hit edge batch shapes through the `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*` path that keeps appearing adjacent to your wedges.

The warmup fix above removes the JIT-during-inference confound you flagged (the D512 kernels are now pre-warmed), so the late `_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_state_kernel` JITs should disappear — one less variable. Please post the stacks when you have them; the all-ranks `--native` dump is what we need.

Update — deployed 28fef2c703, then caught the wedge live with native stacks. It's not a collective stall and not a CUDA deadlock — it's an in-inference Triton JIT-compile cascade.

First: your warmup import fix works. On our 4×GB10/SM121 TP4 box the Warming up DeepSeek V4 D512-split… line now fires and startup JITs are 0 (was self-skipping via the stale import). Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Then we caught a wedge in the act. py-spy --native is dead on this aarch64 box (UNW_EBADREG from libunwind), so for C-stacks I used gdb -p <pid> -ex "set sysroot /proc/<pid>/root" -ex "thread apply all bt" — the sysroot makes gdb symbolize the in-container libs. All 4 Worker_TP ranks + EngineCore, captured while paused.

The decisive part — rank0 was progressing, not stuck.

rank0 first sample — blocked in a stream sync triggered by a .item():
cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda) → cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart)
 → at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda                     # .item() GPU→CPU readback
 (py) _c128a_effective_topk_width  sparse_mla.py:384        # max_pos = int(positions.max().item())
    → build_c128a_topk_metadata → _build_attention_metadata → execute_model
rank0 re-sampled ~3 min later — moved into Triton compilation:
llvm::Module::print / AssemblyWriter::printFunction  (libtriton.so)   # LLVM codegen
…later: cuLaunchKernelEx → __triton_launcher…launch()
rank1, rank2: cuStreamSynchronize (waiting on the stream/peer). rank3: cuLaunchKernelEx → __triton_launcher. EngineCore: acquire_read → get_response (the shm-broadcast wait — the symptom, just waiting on the busy worker). GPUs at the wedge: mixed 10–96% util / 18–86 W (not the uniform full-spin of a HW/collective deadlock).

Conclusion: rank0 moving sync → LLVM codegen → kernel launch proves it isn't deadlocked — it's grinding through JIT compiles. Zero NCCL frames on any rank ⇒ not a collective stall. It's a slow in-inference Triton compile cascade that oscillates: compile → tokens flow → next uncovered shape → stall. So both hypotheses (collective mismatch, CUDA deadlock) are refuted for this wedge.

Why the warmup fix didn't end it: 0 startup JITs, but Triton specializes per shape/stride, and a 1M-context variable-length workload keeps producing new specializations that JIT mid-inference. 16 distinct kernels have JIT-compiled during inference since startup, each exactly once (so the in-process cache works — this is coverage, not a cache bug):
_indexed_d512_split_score / _split_stats / _split_value
_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_acc / _chunked_merge_state
_accumulate_indexed_attention_chunk_multihead
_fp8_mqa_logits / _fp8_paged_mqa_logits_rowwise / _combine_topk_swa_indices
_compute_prefill_metadata / _build_prefill_chunk_metadata
eagle_step_slot_mapping_metadata / eagle_prepare_next_token_padded
_mtp_shared_head_rmsnorm / _tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm / _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum
Stalls cluster on the C128A-metadata path and the chunked-merge kernels.

Likely reframe of the earlier "silent wedges": we had no native stacks for those (ptrace was off then), but this strongly suggests they were the same cascade — our compile cache is ephemeral (/tmp, wiped each restart) and our 2-min watchdog restarted at ~4–6 min, i.e. mid-compile, so they looked permanent and "JIT-free" (jit_monitor only logs a compile after it completes; a kill mid-ptxas/codegen never logs).

Our side: persisting the Triton/Inductor cache to a durable bind so the shape set accumulates across restarts instead of re-paying every time. (We also wired an on-demand NCCL flight-recorder dump into the watchdog in case a true collective stall ever appears — but this wasn't one.)

Questions:
1. Can warmup be extended to the runtime shapes of these kernels — especially the C128A-metadata path and the chunked-merge kernels? Or is the specialization space too large to enumerate (→ persistent cache + accepting first-touch compiles is the realistic path)?
2. _c128a_effective_topk_width does int(positions.max().item()) — a data-dependent device→host sync on the hot path. It's where the CPU first blocks on pending GPU work, but it's also a per-step sync that kills CPU/GPU overlap. Could that max be hoisted/precomputed to drop the sync?
3. Any knob to bound the prefill shape space (fixed chunk sizing / padding) so warmup can be complete?

Happy to share the full all-ranks gdb dumps.

> warmup: add batch=3 to MTP uniform decode kernel warmup jasl/vllm#23

I'll check this Friday

@jasl Got some updates from further soak testing on my 4x Spark Cluster and a question about SM120 prefill throughput...

Resolution of the silent-wedge thread + packed-prefill validation

Following up on the silent worker-wedge we reported. With native stacks (gdb, since py-spy --native is UNW_EBADREG on aarch64), we refuted both the NCCL-collective and CUDA-deadlock hypotheses — caught all 4 ranks with rank0 progressing cuStreamSynchronize → llvm::Module::print (Triton LLVM codegen) → cuLaunchKernelEx. It's a Triton JIT-compile cascade in the D512 chunked sparse-MLA prefill, not a deadlock — long-context prefills hit uncovered kernel shapes that compile mid-inference; our watchdog was killing them mid-ptxas, which made them look permanent.

The fix is your own VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL flag (currently off-by-default). Enabling it routes prefill through the FlashInfer _SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner instead of the Triton path. We validated it correctness-first on GB10/SM121, TP4:
- Needle-in-haystack retrieval correct on both 4.4K- and 48K-token chunked prefills (vs the Triton baseline); deterministic math/primes match.
- 48K chunked prefill → 0 new JITs (Triton path fires the _indexed_d512_chunked_merge/split cascade here).
- 2.5h soak: JIT count flat, zero D512 prefill JITs, no wedge/crash.

It eliminates the prefill-JIT class entirely and moots the D512-split warmup machinery. Would you consider promoting it to default for SM12x? Happy to share full logs.

One open question: even with packed prefill, a single large-context prefill monopolizes the engine (~26s for ~48K, concurrent requests block) — each chunk is a heavy multi-second step that doesn't yield to decodes. Is there planned work on SM120 prefill throughput or mid-chunk scheduling?

Doing some more testing, curious to see if there's any way to tune the kernel to improve prefill latency:

Long-context prefill on GB10 (sm_120) is memory/latency-bound — request: a dense prefill path that skips the indexer's KV scan

Running DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 4× DGX Spark GB10 (sm_120, TP=4) on the sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview line, with VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1 + ..._PREFILL=1 (packed FlashInfer). The packed prefill has been great — eliminated the D512 Triton JIT cascade, 0 in-inference JITs, correct at 150K (needle retrieval ✓). Thank you.

The remaining pain is fresh-context prefill latency: request_prefill_time_seconds p99 ≈ 240 s for ~500K-token cache-miss prefills (TTFT p99 ≈ 640 s when one is queued behind another). A controlled 153K fresh prefill measured 102 s ≈ 0.66 ms/token (→ ~4.5 min at 415K).

Profile (4-node, nvidia-smi -l 2 across the prefill):
- SM clock pinned ~2450–2500 MHz (near max) throughout
- Power only ~63 W avg / 79 W peak vs ~86 W ceiling, oscillating down to ~37 W between chunks
- Identical on all 4 ranks; decode for contrast profiles flat ~37 W (NCCL spin-wait)

Read: clocks maxed but power well under ceiling + heavy oscillation ⇒ memory/latency-bound (idle-waiting on LPDDR5X ~273 GB/s), not compute-bound — there's real headroom the kernels aren't capturing.

Ask (in order of effort):
1. Is a dense prefill path feasible? DSA's lightning indexer is fundamentally a decode optimization (sparse KV reads during gen). During prefill we populate full KV anyway, and the indexer adds an O(N²)-ish scoring scan on top — a strong suspect for the memory stalls. A prefill that runs attention densely (reuse the existing packed/FlashMLA dense path) and builds the index lazily would skip that scan and needs no new sm_120 kernel — it's scheduling/routing. Could you confirm whether the indexer scan dominates prefill traffic (an nsys range would isolate indexer vs attention), and whether a dense-prefill toggle is in scope?
2. Indexer/attention/merge fusion to cut LPDDR5X round-trips.
3. Noting use_fp4_indexer_cache is hard-gated to sm_10x (indexer.py:274-283) — it'd help here but needs an sm_120 FP4-indexer port (third_party/fmha_sm100 only). Lower priority given the effort.

Happy to run any profiling config you'd like reproduced on real GB10 hardware.

@wingcomm — consolidating replies to your three write-ups (the gdb wedge diagnosis, the packed-prefill validation, and the cache-miss prefill profile). Thank you for all of it — the native-stack work on aarch64 especially is the kind of evidence that's hard to get and easy to misattribute.

### 1. The wedge = in-inference Triton JIT cascade, and the `.item()` sync — fixed & shipped

Confirmed against the code on every point. `int(positions.max().item())` in `_c128a_effective_topk_width` (`models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py`) is a real per-step device→host sync on the C128A metadata path — and it's now **gone**: it sources the max position from the CPU-side `CommonAttentionMetadata.max_seq_len` instead (no sync; decode value is identical, only chunked prefill sees a safe slightly-wider 128-aligned top-k). It's in the latest validated head, tag `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260626` (`c766cbc6ff`), GSM8K + long-context coherence revalidated. Thanks for flagging it.

On extending warmup (Q1/Q3): for **stock DSv4-Flash** the prefill kernel shape space is already finite and warmup-complete — `combined_topk` is fixed at 640 regardless of context length, and the D512-split warmup enumerates the full `{256…1152}` set. The chunked-merge kernels (`_indexed_d512_chunked_merge_*`) are the one un-warmed family, but they only fire when `combined_topk > 1152`, and DSv4-Flash caps at 640 — so on stock DSv4-Flash they should be unreachable. **Question back:** did your gdb actually catch the *merge* kernels compiling, or only the split + C128A-metadata ones? If you genuinely saw merge-kernel codegen at 1M/TP4, something's escaping the 640 cap on your config and we'd want your `combined_topk` / `window_size`. (The C128A *metadata kernel* itself is already JIT-stable — one compile — so the stall clustered there is the `.item()` sync stalling the launch stream around the *downstream* compiles, not a metadata recompile.) Persisting the Triton cache to a durable bind is the right belt-and-suspenders regardless.

### 2. Promoting packed prefill (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL`) — we want to, and your soak moves it forward

Our own DeepSeek-reference replay agrees with you: on the compressed-KV (C4A) layers packed matches the reference for non-first prefills (cosine ~0.96) while the default FlashMLA combine diverges (~0.56–0.74, stale workspace) — so packed is the *more*-correct path, and the `≤64`-scratch case under MTP plus the "84-vs-83" padding case are both already handled in code. The one thing we owe before flipping the default: the flag was shelved on a single signal — GSM8K at concurrency 8 came in ~0.90 (packed) vs ~0.95 (FlashMLA), and that measurement didn't include MTP. Your needle + 2.5 h flat-JIT soak demonstrate retrieval correctness and stability but not that aggregate-accuracy-under-concurrency number, so our gate to promote is a **GSM8K nc=8 with MTP** re-run; our replay predicts parity.

One implementation caveat worth stating: this flag only activates when the FlashInfer-SM120 sparse-MLA kernel is present — stock vLLM wheels don't ship it (`is_deep_gemm_supported()` is False and released flashinfer has no `_sparse_mla_sm120`), which is exactly why it's opt-in and why our stock validation boxes default to Marlin (W4A16, GSM8K-correct on both SM120 and SM121). So "promote to default" means default-on *when the kernel is present*; stock-deps users are unaffected.

On a single large prefill monopolizing the engine: that's stock vLLM-v1 chunked prefill, not DSv4-specific (no DSv4 scheduler). Today's only lever is a smaller `long_prefill_token_threshold` — finer chunks interleave decodes more often, at some prefill-throughput cost. True mid-chunk yielding is upstream scheduler work we don't have in flight in this PR.

### 3. Cache-miss prefill latency — your memory-bound read is right; dense-prefill isn't free, but fusion is the win

Confirmed from the code: during prefill the SM120 indexer top-k is **two-pass** — it materializes the full `(num_q, seq_len_kv)` **fp32** logits in global memory then re-reads them in a separate top-k pass. For a ~150K prefill that's hundreds of MB of fp32 logits written-then-read **per layer** over ~273 GB/s — exactly your "clocks pinned, power well under ceiling, oscillating between chunks" signature.

But a dense-prefill toggle isn't pure routing: the compressed-layer prefill attention is data-dependent on the indexer top-k (`_forward_prefill` reads `topk_indices_buffer` / `c128a_prefill_topk_indices` → `combined_indices`, and the kernel gathers *only* those slots). There's no full-context dense MLA prefill kernel in-tree (the only index-free path is the 4096-token SWA window), and "dense + lazy index" changes DSA's intended prefill semantics — a correctness-bearing kernel project, not a flag.

**The better lever is your #2 (fusion):** a fused score+top-k kernel that keeps the M×N scores in SRAM and emits only the top-k indices would kill the dominant LPDDR5X round-trip with no semantics change. We can quantify the share first — **happy to run an nsys indexer-vs-attention range-split on our 2-node GB10** and post it; the ops are cleanly separable in the timeline. On the FP4 indexer (#3): correct it's hard-gated to sm_10x, and the sm120 FP8 topk fallback also early-returns for FP4 Q — so it's a kernel port (q-side FP4 quant exists; no sm120 FP4 logits/top-k *consumer*). This is the analysis:

**Fatal `operation not permitted` from un-warmed Triton specialization of `_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel` (o_proj) on unaligned prefill chunks**

**Env:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SM120 / `NVIDIA_GB10` (DGX Spark), 2-node TP=2 (cross-node), fp8 KV, MTP spec-decode (`num_speculative_tokens=2`), chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`), `enforce_eager=False` (`cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). vLLM `v20260621.dev284+g76dff54c2`.

**Symptom:** a TP worker dies mid-inference; the peer rank then blocks in the cross-node collective until its `sample_tokens` RPC times out (~5 min) → `EngineDeadError` and the whole server shuts down.

```text
models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py -> fp8_einsum.py:145 _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel[grid](...)
triton/compiler/compiler.py:465 _init_handles -> driver.active.utils.load_binary(...)
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: operation not permitted
```

**Trigger:** the failing step is the **tail chunk of a chunked prefill** — prompt 266,603 tokens, prefix-cache hit, remainder scheduled = **1131 tokens**. `1131 % 16 = 11`.

**Root cause:** the o_proj einsum (and the other prefill kernels) is Triton-specialized on the `num_tokens` divisibility-by-16 predicate. `_deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup` only warms `num_tokens = prefill_tokens` (= `max_num_batched_tokens`, a multiple of 16), so **only the divisible-by-16 specialization is compiled/loaded during warmup**. The first real prefill chunk whose token count is not a multiple of 16 JIT-loads the *unaligned* variant during inference; `load_binary` returns `cudaErrorNotPermitted`, which the driver raises when a module load coincides with CUDA-graph stream capture in the process — so it is fatal rather than a latency spike.

This is consistent with `jit_monitor` already warning earlier in the same run (non-fatal, before any capture) for exactly these kernels:

```text
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel
... _w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm, _tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_kernel,
... _build_prefill_chunk_metadata_kernel, _compute_prefill_metadata_kernel
```

i.e. the warmup already intends to keep these out of the inference path (the chunked-prefill and D512-split dummies), it just misses the `% 16 != 0` class.

> The odd-sized batch in our case followed a `Missing cached draft probabilities ... falling back to legacy speculative rejection behavior` warning, but the fatal kernel is a generic prefill kernel — any unaligned prefill chunk reproduces it regardless of spec-decode.

**Suggested fix:** in `_deepseek_v4_sparse_mla_attention_warmup`, add an unaligned-token prefill dummy run mirroring the existing aligned pair, so the unaligned specialization compiles outside capture:

```python
unaligned = prefill_tokens - 1 if prefill_tokens % 16 == 0 else prefill_tokens
if unaligned > 1 and unaligned % 16 != 0:
    runner._dummy_run(num_tokens=unaligned, skip_eplb=True, is_profile=True,
                      force_attention=True, create_single_prefill=True)
    runner._dummy_run(num_tokens=unaligned, skip_eplb=True, is_profile=True,
                      force_attention=True, create_single_prefill=True,
                      profile_seq_lens=unaligned * 2)
```

I am trying the patch now, will take some time to see if this solves it for sure.

Thanks for the excellent analysis — the root cause is exactly right: the o_proj `_deepseek_v4_sm12x_fp8_einsum_kernel` JIT-loads a fresh cubin for the prefill chunk's token count, and when that `cuModuleLoad` lands during CUDA-graph capture it returns `cudaErrorNotPermitted` and kills the worker (which then hangs the cross-node peer in the collective → `EngineDeadError`). The `jit_monitor` warnings are the harmless *compile* hook; the fatal path is the cubin *load*, which it doesn't cover — that's why you saw warnings earlier in the run but a crash later.

One correction that matters for the fix, though: it's **not** a `% 16` divisibility class. `num_tokens` is declared `tl.constexpr` in that kernel, so it specializes on the **exact** token count (plus three input strides that scale with it: `a_stride_group = T·d` and the two scale strides via `align(T,4)`). So warming `prefill_tokens - 1` only pre-compiles the single size 8191 — a real tail of 1131 (or any other) is a different cubin and still JITs mid-inference. Enumerating tail sizes in warmup can't work either, since the tail size is effectively continuous.

The robust fix is a one-kernel edit: demote `num_tokens` (and those three token-dependent stride args) from `tl.constexpr` to runtime args. `num_tokens` is used only for masking, the loop is over `hidden_size`, and the grid is host-computed via `cdiv`, so it's numerically identical and perf-neutral — and it collapses the kernel to a **single cubin for all chunk sizes**, so the existing 8192 warmup then covers everything. (This mirrors what the kernel's own producer `_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant_per_head` already does.)

Good news on scope: o_proj is the **only** DeepSeek-V4 prefill kernel with this constexpr-on-token-count pattern — the others take the token dim as a runtime arg or via the grid, so they're not at risk of this particular crash.

### Packed FlashInfer SM120 prefill hangs the GPU on multi-request prefill batches (silent engine wedge)

Reporting a reproducible hard wedge on the packed FlashInfer SM120 **prefill** path (`VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`), which became default-on in `fd76d65d4`. Captured live across all ranks. **Still reproduces against the current PR tip** (history through `367ed7c66`); it is a **distinct failure mode** from the recently-landed prefill fixes — see "Not the same as…" below.

**Environment**
- 4× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=4 / EP=4, RoCE CX7 fabric, vLLM-native `torch.distributed` (no Ray)
- Build: this PR's `sm120-pr-41834-stable-preview-20260626` snapshot (`c766cbc6`), FlashInfer 0.6.13, CUDA 13.2
- Flags: `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_DECODE=1`, `VLLM_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASHINFER_SM120_PREFILL=1`
